citations.narrative:
The inventory for this current report is a total of 68 animals, upon review of the facility's license it is approved for up to 50
animals. Licenses authorize increments of 50 animals on hand at any single point in time during the period of licensure. A
licensee must obtain a new license before any change resulting in more than the authorized number of animals on hand
at any single point in time during the period of licensure.
Correct by July 28, 2026.

APHIS Officials observed multiple rabbits with signs of heat stress. The rabbits were breathing heavily and panting. The
atmospheric temperature was 96 F, and the rabbits being housed outdoors did not have any type of artificial cooling.
Excessive heat is a risk factor for outdoor rabbits and could have a significant negative health impact on the animals.
When the temperature exceeds 90 F, artificial cooling must be provided to the rabbits by sprinkler system or other means.
Correct by 6pm on July 9, 2026.

The outdoor enclosure of a large gray rabbit was not in good repair. The enclosure had numerous 4-inch-long sharp metal
points that were bent towards the rabbit which may cause injury. Primary enclosures must be kept in good repair to
protect rabbits from injury. The rabbit was moved at the time of the inspection to an enclosure without sharp points.
Correct from this day forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with Facility Representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Sarah Roloff, CS n
